summary_paragraph: A 58-year-old woman was admitted after a mechanical fall resulting in a right trimalleolar ankle fracture and bilateral leg ulcers with cellulitis. She had a history of COPD, diastolic heart failure, diabetes, and polysubstance abuse. Shortly after admission, she developed hypercarbic respiratory failure requiring intubation and mechanical ventilation. She was treated for suspected ventilator-associated pneumonia with vancomycin and piperacillin/tazobactam, and a course of steroids for COPD exacerbation. Due to difficulty weaning, she underwent tracheostomy placement on hospital day 17. She also experienced acute renal failure, likely prerenal from hyperglycemia, which improved with IV fluids; lasix and lisinopril were discontinued. Multifocal atrial tachycardia was managed with metoprolol. Her leg infection resolved with antibiotics, and wound care was continued. She was weaned to a trach collar, mental status improved, and she was transferred to extended care for ongoing rehabilitation and trach management.
